# Canonical Systems Glossary {.unnumbered}

| Term | Operational Systems Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Action Chunking** | Predicting a sequence of $H$ future continuous action steps per neural inference pass to bridge compute latency. |
| **Category 0 Stop** | Uncontrolled emergency stop by immediately disconnecting electrical power to machine actuators (IEC 60204-1). |
| **Category 1 Stop** | Controlled deceleration to a complete stop with electrical power maintained, followed by power disconnection. |
| **Category 2 Stop** | Controlled position hold where power remains continuously supplied to machine actuators. |
| **Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE)** | A formal assurance methodology structuring top-level safety claims into sub-arguments supported by empirical test evidence. |
| **Control Barrier Function (CBF)** | A mathematical constraint ensuring the physical state of a system remains strictly within a safe invariant set for all time. |
| **Cumulative Design Dossier** | An accumulating, versioned engineering record tracking specifications, contracts, and test evidence for a physical system. |
| **Delegated Physical Authority** | The permission granted to an autonomous system to energize actuators and move matter without continuous human physical intervention. |
| **Dual-Brain Architecture** | A systems topology separating best-effort AI proposal computation (Linux MPU) from deterministic real-time safety enforcement (RTOS MCU). |
| **Dynamic Stopping Distance ($d_{\text{stop}}$)** | The total physical clearance required to bring a moving machine to rest, accounting for latency tails and maximum deceleration. |
| **Expiring Intent Lease** | A time-bounded proposal ($t_{\text{expire}}$) defining spatial target envelopes that become invalid if not executed before the lease expires. |
| **Information Age ($\Delta t$)** | The duration elapsed between physical sensor transduction and the moment a computed action energizes an actuator. |
| **Operational Design Domain (ODD)** | The operating conditions (speed, friction, temperature, lighting) under which a physical system is certified to function safely. |
| **Policy Endogeneity** | The feedback property where active neural policy actions dictate which world states the machine encounters, altering future training logs. |
| **Proposal–Permission Split** | The architectural rule establishing that neural models generate unverified proposals, while real-time enforcers permit or veto execution. |
| **Tail Latency ($P_{99}$)** | The 99th percentile execution duration; the primary metric governing real-time safety margins in physical systems. |
| **Temporal Ensembling** | Blending overlapping action trajectories across consecutive inference passes to guarantee $\mathcal{C}^2$ acceleration continuity. |
| **Physical Agent** | An autonomous computational system that couples learned, open-world semantic models to real-time physical actuators, exercising delegated authority over matter and energy under hard physical constraints, non-zero mass, and bounded latency. |
| **Physical AI Kit** | The reference dual-brain hardware testbed (Arduino UNO Q Linux MPU + Real-Time MCU, sensor suite, and precision motion stage) used to construct and evaluate physical agents. |
| **Unsafe Control Action (UCA)** | A control command issued too late, too early, out of order, or with excessive magnitude that leads to a physical hazard (STPA). |
